youtube_title: Why Don't Satellites Fall Down? How Orbits Work
youtube_description:
Why don't satellites fall down? They do: an orbiting spacecraft is always falling toward Earth, but it moves sideways so fast that the curve of its fall matches the curve of Earth.

At the space station's height, gravity is still about 90 percent as strong as on the ground. The station travels at about 17,500 mph and circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes. Astronauts float because they're falling right along with it.
